subject: Nimbus Health: migration windows, exception asks, and comms matrix
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-11-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Nimbus Health: migration windows, exception asks, and comms matrix

Team —

Nimbus Health is scheduled to move from redwood-infer-v1 -> redwood-infer-v2 in Q1. They just surfaced two things we need cross-functional alignment on before I publish the customer notice:

1) A preferred maintenance window request (their ops team asked for a 4-hour window during US-PST nights).
2) One-off exception ask: they want a 90-day data-retention override for token-level logs for an audit that ends Jan 31.

My asks:
- Engineering: confirm whether the switchover we plan (live model swap with traffic mirroring for 48h -> cut) can safely be done inside a 4-hour window, or if we need a phased lane (shorter per-customer windows + fallback).
- Prod Ops (Priyom): can we offer an SLA-safe blue/green with automatic fallback if latency/tail errors spike? If not, propose the minimum safe window.
- Sales/Customer Success (Marissa & Ben): confirm the comm cadence. What will the customer require for advance notice and on-call support during the window?
- Legal/Privacy (Kimberly): quick read on the retention exception: is there a compliance path (signed addendum + limited-scoped retention) or do we need procurement + security sign-off first?

I've attached a first draft switchover matrix (rows = candidate windows; columns = risk, rollback, on-call, extra config). Please review and add redlines. I'll consolidate and send to Nimbus by EOD Monday.

Attachments: nimbus_switchover_matrix_v1.xlsx, customer_notice_v2.md, exception_request_template.docx

Thanks —
Olga
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-13T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health: migration windows, exception asks, and comms matrix

Olga —

Thanks for pulling this together. A few quick notes from GTM perspective:
- Nimbus will expect 2 weeks' formal notice + a follow-up runbook 72h before the window. That was in the SOW.
- For the 4-hour night window: historically they want <2 minute failover for production endpoints. That requirement makes a pure swap risky unless we keep a warmed fallback and traffic split for >24h.

My recommendation: propose two SKUs to the customer:
- Standard cut (4h night window) — requires a warmed fallback and 24h split-mirroring pre-cut.
- Accelerated cut (fast single-window) — requires a short SLA uplift and committed dedicated capacity for the night (extra charge).

I'll draft the customer-facing language if engineering confirms the delta on warm time.

-Ben
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-14T14:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health: migration windows, exception asks, and comms matrix

Folks —

Operational constraints and what I can commit to:
- We can support a 4-hour window if we do the following operationally: warm two standby nodes in dedicated pool, run traffic split 24h prior (98/2) to catch regressions, and keep KV-cache warming scripts running. That adds ~1.5k/month to their bill for reserved hours (we should include as optional line item).
- Automatic fallback: we can flip traffic back to v1 within 10 minutes if token-generation latency exceeds thresholds or error-rate delta > 0.7% sustained for 5 minutes. That meets the <2 minute failover requirement for request routing, but token-level in-flight consistency will be eventual (client retries may be required).
- Exception: data-retention override — operationally trivial to enable scoped logging, but we need Legal + Security approval and a signed addendum. Please coordinate with Kimberly.

Suggested customer language bullet list for the notice:
- Pre-cut: 2 weeks' notice, runbook 72h prior, 24h split mirroring
- Cut window: 4 hours starting at 02:00 PST (example) — target cut at T+2h, observation and rollback guardrails T+2h..T+4h
- Post-cut: 48h elevated monitoring and optional rollback window up to 72h

I'll add the fall-back SLAs and the reserved-hours cost to the matrix and push an updated file to the Drive link.

—Priyom
Head of Prod Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Ava Reynolds <ava@nimbushealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2028-11-15T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health: migration windows, exception asks, and comms matrix

Thanks — forwarding to procurement and looping in our ops lead. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 02:00 PST window is acceptable, but we would prefer the cut occur between 02:00–03:30 local time. If you need a longer observation period post-cut, we can extend the maintenance window provided you keep the endpoint read-only mode for the first hour.
- For the 90-day retention exception: procurement needs a signed addendum and Security will require the exception limit to be scoped to specific log types and IP ranges. Please provide the addendum template ASAP.
